resource_risks.description: The installed shell reads a bundled JSON contract resource and must not keep persistent file handles or depend only on development paths.
resource_risks.mitigation: The Rust command reads the contract with fs::read_to_string, first from Tauri resources and then from development source as fallback, returning a bounded JSON report.

resource_risks.description: The contract declares multiple data accumulation targets that could grow over time if not classified by runtime plane and close-out gate.
resource_risks.mitigation: Accumulation targets are classified into platform_data_store, support_diagnostic_store, and history/evaluation records with provenance requirements, and the runtime data boundary registry declares retention/visibility planes.

resource_risks.description: A project-wide shell restructure could accidentally add a new external sidecar or shell plugin permission without install/security review.
resource_risks.mitigation: No new sidecar or plugin-shell capability was added; default capability remains core-only and the contract records sidecars as requiring a future scoped audit.

lifecycle_checks.create_path: Tauri bundle.resources maps runtime-contracts files into the app resource directory.
lifecycle_checks.cleanup_path: No persistent handle is created; fs::read_to_string closes the file after reading.
One-shot process exits after deterministic checks.
evidence: corepack pnpm --filter platform-desktop-app run check: passed

measurement_checks.metric: contract gates and accumulation target counts
measurement_checks.threshold: 12 required gates and 8 accumulation targets present.

notes: No new long-running process, watcher, timer, network connection, shell sidecar, or global installation was added.
